text:
Sam Patel: SUP-4567 — customer (Acct-489) reporting p99 API latency ~1.2s for text-generation from eu-west since ~03:00 UTC. Any infra or routing changes?

OpsBot: [alert] high p99 observed on route eu-west-gateway at 2026-03-17T03:05Z. Grafana: https://grafana.redwood.internal/d/edge/p95-p99-latency (stacked).

Maria Gomez: i'm on it. quick glance: p95 jumped 90ms -> ~350ms, p99 ~1.15s. Backend srv metrics look normal (CPU/RAM fine). Ingress shows TLS handshake time increase and extra RTTs.

Lee Chen: running traceroutes from eu probes -> seeing an extra hop via uk1-b for a subset of flows. example from probe eu-probe-3:
```
traceroute to api.eu.redwood.net (34.12.45.67), 30 hops max, 60 byte packets
 1  10.10.0.1  0.6 ms  0.5 ms  0.6 ms
 2  203.0.113.5  5.1 ms  4.8 ms  5.0 ms
 3  198.51.100.2  12.3 ms  11.9 ms  12.1 ms
 4  51.15.120.7 (uk1-b-pop)  70.4 ms  72.1 ms  69.8 ms  <-- extra cross-zone hop
 5  34.12.45.67  75.0 ms  74.6 ms  75.1 ms
```

Jordan Carter: dig results show some clients resolving to uk1-b fallback IPs. `dig +short api.eu.redwood.net @8.8.8.8` -> returns mix of 34.12.45.67 (eu-pop-a) and 3.5.9.11 (uk1-b). TTLs are low (2s) so GSLB shifts quickly.

Nina Rossi: TLS handshake p99 jumped from ~30ms -> 200-800ms. That plus extra hop explains the p99 spike. Could be BGP/anycast instability or GSLB health-checks marking eu-pop subsets unhealthy and routing to uk.

Lee Chen: pulled tcpdump for affected src IP (provided by support). SNI shows some flows still target eu SNI but BGP path directs to uk POP causing hairpin. snippet:
```
12:03:21.123456 IP client->34.12.45.67: Flags [S], seq 0, win 64240, options [mss 1460], length 0
12:03:21.124789 IP 3.5.9.11->client: Flags [S.], seq 0, ack 1, win 65535
```

Maria Gomez: checking deploy logs — no control plane or edge deploys since 02:45Z. network partner posted BGP flaps in eu region at ~03:00Z.

Sam Patel: support escalated and updated SUP-4567. Customer asked for immediate mitigation (they're on a production checkout).

Jordan Carter: short-term options: (A) force DNS weight to prefer eu-pop-a for affected zones/IPs; (B) push a BGP community override to prefer eu-pop-a; (C) configure edge to accept session-resume to reduce full handshake rate. A and B have fastest effect.

Lee Chen: i can push BGP community override to signal prefer eu-pop-a for the customer CIDR. will cause transient rebalancing — need signoff.

Nina Rossi: also propose bumping TLS session caching and session ticket reuse for the edge temporarily — reduces handshake overhead for repeated connections. app teams need notify for ticket rotation.

Maria Gomez: plan: 1) Lee applies BGP override for Acct-489 IP range; 2) Jordan updates support messaging and DNS if needed; 3) Maria monitors p95/p99 and ingress handshake times; 4) Nina opens follow-up to harden session reuse.

Sam Patel: approve. Lee proceed and call it out in this thread once done. Jordan keep support updated. Maria/nina monitor graphs.

Lee Chen: pushed override at 03:28Z. change-id bgp-ovr-778.

OpsBot: [deploy] BGP override applied by Lee Chen — bgp-ovr-778. propagation observed across peers.

Maria Gomez: 03:30Z metrics: p95 down to ~120ms, p99 ~420ms and trending down. TLS handshake p99 improved to ~280ms.

support-team: updated SUP-4567 and notified customer; they reported noticeable improvement and confirmed lower latency on their checkout flow. :relieved:

Nina Rossi: follow-ups (owner):
- add route-affinity drift alert (Maria)
- increase TLS session reuse TTL / document ticket rotation (Nina)
- review GSLB healthcheck thresholds to avoid premature failover (Jordan)
- coordinate with network partner on BGP instability RCA (Lee)

Sam Patel: thanks everyone. if metrics reflare we escalate to full postmortem. for now keeping the override in place for 30m then gradual rollback once stable.

Maria Gomez: noted — i'll watch for 30m then schedule rollback window.

Lee Chen: ack. rolling back at 04:00Z if stable.

support-team: SUP-4567 -> customer closed for now, will reopen if issue returns.
